title: Mourners march on City Hall: Shooting death inquiry demanded
article: Moments before burying Deng Kuol -- the Calgary man fatally shot by a police officer last month -- friends of the Sudanese immigrant marched to City Hall, calling for an independent judicial inquiry into his death.

About 200 members of the city's Sudanese community left the 34- year-old's funeral in the northeast Friday morning, walking downtown to deliver letters to the mayor and police chief seeking the inquiry.
Kuol died Oct. 25 after a violent struggle with Const. Ira Macumber, a local police officer called to a Forest Lawn apartment building to escort Kuol from the premises.
Kuol refused to leave and allegedly used a knife to slash the 40- year-old officer in the arm, before Macumber fired two shots into his neck.
"The Sudanese community believes that there was no justification for the ultimate use of the deadly force," said Martin Yak, a spokesman for the group.
"We are asking for justice . . . we want the Alberta government to set up an independent inquiry."
Neither police Chief Jack Beaton nor Mayor Dave Bronconnier was available for comment.
An Alberta Justice spokesman, however, said an independent fatality inquiry into Kuol's death is mandatory and will begin as soon as the Calgary Police Service completes its own investigation.
"They will essentially get what they are asking for," Michael Shields said from Edmonton. "Judicial independence is certainly an integral part of the fatality inquiry."
A provincial court judge presides over such an inquiry, makes recommendations and writes a report for the public. However, a fatality inquiry does not make any legal findings or assign blame.
Friends of Kuol's have repeatedly questioned the chain of events that led to his death, saying Kuol wasn't a violent man.
However, he was wanted by RCMP in Brooks for breach of probation regarding a drunk-driving conviction.

A provincial court judge in Calgary issued a warrant for Kuol's arrest on Oct. 14 after failing to appear to face charges of assaulting a peace officer and not complying with an order to abstain from alcohol.
It was alleged that on June 2 Kuol assaulted Calgary Const. L Garry Basso.
And Calgary EMS confirmed Macumber was treated immediately after the incident for a gash to the underside of his left bicep.
Emotions ran high outside City Hall Friday as friends lamented Kuol's death, particularly since he had escaped war-ravaged Sudan in the 1980s.
"Deng didn't need to run away from the war in Sudan to come and die in Canada," said an emotional Sidonia Amel, who grew up with Kuol in Bor, Sudan, and escaped to Cuba with him in the '80s.
"If he has a gun and they shoot him, I understand. If he has a knife, I don't see a need to shoot him two times. If they shoot him once, he's helpless."
Kuol came to Canada in 1997 after spending 15 years in Cuba, where he fled after his mother and father were killed in his country's long-running civil war.
He moved to Red Deer and later to Brooks, where he worked at a meat-packing plant. At the time of his death, he was unemployed and in Calgary.
According to Jok Mach, Kuol has two sisters still living in a refugee camp in Kenya.
"I have known him since he was born and . . . I didn't expect him to die like this," Mach said following the funeral. "The way he died was not proper. He didn't threaten anyone's life."
City police officials said they won't comment further until the investigation is complete.
